blocks.tamil_translation: When Rasulullah ﷺ said, “Avoid sitting on the paths,” the Sahabah (RA) said, “O Rasulullah, sometimes we have to sit on the paths. We are compelled to sit there and talk.” Rasulullah ﷺ said, “If you must sit like that, then fulfil the rights of the passers-by.” When the Sahabah asked, “O Rasulullah, what are the rights of the passers-by (those using the footpath)?' Rasulullah ﷺ replied, “Lowering the gaze, removing harmful things from the path (or not causing harm oneself), replying to the salam, enjoining good and forbidding evil.”” Hazrat Abu Sa'id Khudri (RA) narrates this.

blocks.text:
Explanation:- The intention of the Sahabah was this: it is not possible for us to avoid sitting on the paths, because we do not have enough space to hold our gatherings. Therefore, wherever a few of us meet, we sit down right there on the path; we also consult among ourselves about our worldly and religious matters, we ask about one another's condition, if any of us falls ill we decide about his treatment, and if there is any bitterness among us we make peace, remove the wrong thoughts that have arisen in the mind and purify our hearts.
(Mazahir-e-Haq)

blocks.arabic_text: عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ﵄ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ: لَيْسَ مِنَّا مَنْ لَمْ يَرْحَمْ صَغِيرَنَا وَيُوَقِّرْ كَبِيرَنَا وَيَأْمُرْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه الترمذي وقال: هذا حديث حسن غريب ، باب ما جاء في رحمة الصبيان، رقم:١٩٢١
